items.title: Cursor agents gain Computer Use to control local desktop apps
facts: Cursor's local agent can now click and type across any desktop app, driving tools like the iOS Simulator to verify the code it writes.
Developers can invoke Computer Use by adding @Computer Use to a prompt. Cursor may also select the tool automatically when a task requires interaction with a visual interface.
The feature is available by updating the desktop app. Cursor announced no accompanying pricing change.
Previously available only in cloud agents' isolated VMs or self-hosted workers, not the local IDE.

x_posts.author: @cursor_ai
x_posts.text:
Cursor can now control your computer.

Agents can drive desktop apps like the iOS Simulator to test the features they build.

x_posts.author: @cursor_ai
x_posts.text:
Computer Use lets agents click and type across any app on your computer, not just the browser.

Cursor uses it on its own when a task needs it. You can also ask for it by @-mentioning Computer Use in your prompt.

Update Cursor to try it: https://cursor.com/download

items.why_hot: Official announcement of Computer Use for local agents, enabling end-to-end testing in apps like iOS Simulator, with massive engagement on the posts.
items.reaction: Users note it closes the loop for mobile development by letting agents test features themselves; some highlight the need for caution with real desktop access.

items.title: Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro with strong Terminal-Bench coding scores
facts: We're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%).
Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. The full model weights will be released by Nov 4.
It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities.

x_posts.text:

items.why_hot: Launch of a high-performing open-weight model scoring near Claude Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench, with emphasis on full-project coding and agentic work.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.310 adds Monitor tool and multiple reliability fixes
facts: Added the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled; long foreground sleeps are now blocked there too.
Fixed requests failing behind some gateways and compatible servers that reject the effort-2025-11-24 beta value or mid-conversation system messages; Claude Code now retries without them.
Fixed compaction after a "Prompt is too long" error keeping too much of a conversation with dense text, such as base64 or SVG, so the next request could fail again.
Improved auto mode's prompt before the first read outside the working directories: it now says when blocking those reads makes shell commands ask for permission.
items.why_hot: Routine but relevant release for a leading coding agent, adding monitoring and fixing reliability issues in non-interactive and cloud sessions.

items.title: Cloudflare security-audit skill trends as AI bug hunter for coding agents
facts: A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.
This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness.
Install with: npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill --skill security-audit

x_posts.author: @NikandrSurkov
x_posts.text:
🛡️ Cloudflare's AI bug hunter is the #1 repo on GitHub today, and after the week we just had, it's the first thing I'd point at my own code.

It's a skill called security-audit that runs inside your coding agent. Cloudflare says it's the starting point of the vulnerability harness it now runs on its own code, where it ended up with 7,245 actionable findings, each with a working test and a draft patch.

How it works:
- maps your architecture, trust boundaries and every input
- sends separate hunter agents after each part of the code
- gives every finding to a fresh agent that tries to disprove it
- writes a report: confirmed, needs validation, rejected

Two tips from the README: run it more than once, because a single run found about half of what repeated runs found. And give it a sandbox with no network, otherwise it won't execute your code to confirm a finding.

items.why_hot: Trending on GitHub as a practical multi-agent skill for security audits inside existing coding agents, with users highlighting its verification process.
items.reaction: Posters describe the multi-phase approach with independent verification agents and recommend sandboxed runs for confirmation.

items.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API adds totals_by_client for tools like OpenCode
facts: The Copilot usage metrics API now reports model usage from more of the tools your developers use with Copilot, including tools like OpenCode that weren’t previously captured in your reports. A new totals_by_client array is available in the enterprise, organization, enterprise-user, and organization-user 1-day and 28-day reports.
Each totals_by_client entry represents one client and includes client, request_count, session_count, token_usage, and totals_by_model.
More developers now use Copilot as the model provider behind tools outside the IDE. Counting requests on the server closes that gap.
items.why_hot: Update improves visibility into how Copilot models are used across different client tools and agents.
